method: Instruction listings decoded directly from the PE bytes of the identified executable through its section table, with the executable size and SHA-256 verified first. Every cited instruction address, operand, name literal, holder vftable cell, data cell and call target was compared with those listings by a second pass that re-read the bytes. Callers were enumerated by scanning the .text section for rel32 call and jmp instructions, so virtual and indirect callers are not covered. Addresses are absolute virtual addresses. The MEASURED facts are call-site and script counts that agree with xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json. Script argument counts, return counts and constants come from a local Lua 5.1 bytecode scan that no tracked artifact carries and are INFERRED. No decompiled body is a tracked evidence dependency.
scope: Static Lua call contracts of the thirteen ItemBase registrations that read an item record or its reference (_getMaxStack, _isStackable, _isRare, _getOwner, _isLocking, _getLockingInfo, _isDealing, _isAttached, _getDealingInfo, _getDealingAttached, _isTrading, _isEquipping, _getEquippingSlot) and of the CharaBase registration _getExtendedTemporaryItem. Each row gives the registration site, receiver type check, declared argument and return lists, the Lua pushes of every branch including an absent item record, the item record fields it reads, failure behavior and yield behavior. Client-side contracts do not establish item identifiers, stack sizes, rare flags, lock tags, dealing values, package numbers or server behavior.
evidenceTier: MIXED, see tierVocabulary and the tier of each fact

framework.reference: manifests/scheduler_item_native_call_contract.json framework and manifests/chara_desktop_native_call_contract.json framework: registration, the 0x00CC9D60 type registry, argument marshalling through 0x00D19A20, the holder receiver adapter, the cell tags, the invalid-parameter route, the return pushers, the world object chain and the item package model. Each registrar builds the return list first and the argument list second.

registration.note: The order of a native is its position among the rel32 calls of its switchboard, counted from 1. Each registrar has one rel32 caller in .text, recorded as registrarCaller. The ItemBase switchboard has 20 calls. The orders 1, 4, 6, 7, 9, 10 and 17 are the natives of the nameplate, binding map and scheduler contracts.

framework.holdersNote: Each invoke routine casts the receiver with 0x009DA6CC from LuaControl (0x01270B4C) to the target type descriptor. A null cast returns false without calling the callback, so a receiver that is not an ItemBase reaches none of the item callbacks.

itemReference.lookup: 0x006F51A0 returns the package manager at owner +0xD8. facts.claim: The callback compares the dword at receiver +0x68 with the dword at 0x00FE0508 and pushes nil through 0x00748920 on equality.

It then compares the key with the dword at 0x00FE0514. On equality it takes R from 0x00CC7510 on ExecuteParameters +0x04, Y = [[R]+0x04] and the object pointer stored at Y +0x124, reads the dword at that object +0x04 through 0x00714270, resolves it with 0x00CC7A50 on ExecuteParameters +0x04, casts the result with 0x009DA6CC from LuaControl 0x01270B4C to CharaBase 0x012709A4 and pushes it through 0x00748B30.
Any other key passes the address of receiver +0x64 to 0x00748B30, which dereferences it, so the pushed control is the owner dword that every other ItemBase callback gives to 0x006F51A0.

The key 0xFC marks an item whose owner is not the chara that holds the package, as in a trade partner. The role comes from the shared use of 0x00FE0514 in _isTrading and from the native name. The writer of the world object Y +0x124 was not traced.

The callback compares the mode byte with the bytes at 0x00FE049D, 0x00FE049F and 0x00FE049E, which hold 0, 2 and 1. A mode equal to the byte at 0x00FE049D (0) takes the three nil exit, and so does a mode that matches none of the three bytes.

Mode 1 takes the byte at bits 16 to 23 of attached1 as the package key and the word at bits 0 to 15 as the slot. It passes the key address and the slot without a decrement to 0x006EE480 for a receiver variant byte of 1 or 0x006EE3E0 otherwise, on the package manager of the receiver owner. A result of 0 pushes three nils.

A record found is turned into a control by 0x006E2770 with the vm pointer from ExecuteParameters +0x04, the record and the flag 0. The control is pushed through 0x00748B30, followed by two nils through 0x00748920.

The three attribute fields come from the wire record: the byte at wire +0x13, the dword at +0x14, the byte at +0x12 and the dword at +0x18 reach attribute +0x20, +0x24, +0x21 and +0x28 through 0x00769760 and are copied to record +0x8C by 0x007698E0.

facts.claim: The callback 0x00708840 builds a stack ItemBase with 0x006DD450, calls the helper 0x00702400 with the ExecuteParameters pointer, the receiver and the flag 1, and destroys the stack object through 0x006DD4D0. _getItem calls the same helper with the flag 0.
The helper reads cell 0 and cell 1 through 0x005819A0 after size tests that call 0x009D22B4 for fewer than one and two cells, and subtracts 1 from each through 0x0078BC90 and 0x0078BCD0.

It calls 0x006F51A0 on the receiver, finds the package with 0x006E5BA0 at 0x0070249D and discards the result with no branch on it, calls 0x006F51A0 again and then calls 0x006EE3E0 with the key address and slot. It never calls 0x006EE480, whatever the flag. A result of 0 pushes nil through 0x00748920.
A record found goes to 0x006E2770 with the vm pointer from ExecuteParameters +0x04, the record and the flag. The returned control is pushed through 0x00748B30.

0x006E2770 reads the descriptor pointer at record +0x08, which holds a target pointer and a slot dword. The first dword of the target goes to ItemBase +0x64, the dword at target +0x04 to +0x68 and the slot dword to +0x6C. The byte at +0x70 is set to 1 when the byte at target +0x21 is 0. The flag only chooses among three wrappers of 0x00CD9360, namely 0x00CC80A0 for 0 and 0x00CC81E0 or 0x00CC8140 for nonzero, as 0x00758EC0 decides. The stored fields do not depend on the flag.

The control reaches later ItemBase natives with a variant byte that the package decides. A package whose record has the byte 0 at +0x21 is looked up through the tree at manager +0x14 and any other package through the tree at +0x08. Which packages carry each value was not traced.

boundaries: These are static client observations. No live Lua call or retail-client walk was performed.
Each registrar has one rel32 caller in .text, recorded as registrarCaller. The run-time order of registration is the switchboard order of the framework.

Script call-site counts are static presence in the shipped scripts. They do not establish which natives a given script reaches at run time. The index counts 14 sites in commanddebugger/commanddebuggerdev that hold a native name as a string constant, and the bytecode scan does not resolve how that script calls them.

The callbacks that dereference a lookup result without a test were not run with an absent record. The reads at the addresses 0x0000007C, 0x00000088, 0x00000090 and 0x00000094 have an unknown run-time effect.

The slot loops of _isTrading, _isEquipping and _getEquippingSlot call a lookup that throws the invalid vector subscript message for an index past the end of a package vector. The package vector sizes for the keys 0xFD, 0xFC and 0xFE were not traced, so the throw was not shown to be reachable.
The writers of the static data object fields at record +0x7C, +0x80, +0x88 and +0x89, and the values that the shipped item data gives them, were not traced.
The roles of the package keys 0xFF, 0xFE, 0xFD and 0xFC, the writer of the world object Y +0x124 and the meaning of the tag numbers other than 0xC9 and 0xCA are INFERRED from native names or unknown.
Whether a null control pushed through 0x00748B30 reaches Lua as nil was not traced. The fade, actor and group contracts record the same boundary.
The server values of the tag vector, the attached dwords and the mode byte come from the wire record that the Bazaar contract describes. This record does not establish which values a server sends.
